column2: On the authority of Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah the Exalted be pleased with them both) that the Messenger of Allah (Allah the Exalted bless him and his family and grant them peace) said: “I have been commanded to fight the people until they testify that there is no god but Allah

and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah, establish the prayer and give the zakāh. If they do that, they have protected their blood and their wealth from me, except by the right of Islam, and their reckoning is with Allah the Exalted.” Reported by al-Bukhārī and Muslim.
His words, “I have been commanded”: the one who commanded the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is Allah,

since there is none other than Him to command him. When a Companion says, “We were commanded to do such-and-such” or “We were forbidden such-and-such”, the one who commanded or forbade them is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died and Abū Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) became caliph, and some of the Arabs apostatised and some refused to pay the zakāh, Abū Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) resolved to fight them,

on the basis that paying the zakāh is part of the right of the two testimonies. He did not have the version of the hadith that adds the prayer and the zakāh to the two testimonies, as this hadith does, and ʿUmar debated with him about it.
The debate between them is reported in the hadith of Abū Hurayrah in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim (20). He said: “When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died and Abū Bakr became caliph after him,
and some of the Arabs disbelieved, ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said to Abū Bakr: How can you fight the people when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has said:

‘I have been commanded to fight the people until they say: There is no god but Allah. Whoever says there is no god but Allah has protected his wealth and his life from me, except by its right, and their reckoning is with Allah the Exalted’? Abū Bakr said: By Allah,
I will certainly fight whoever separates the prayer from the zakāh,
for zakāh is the right due on wealth. By Allah,
if they withheld from me even a hobbling cord that they used to give to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I would fight them for withholding it. ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: By Allah,
it was only that I saw that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, had opened Abū Bakr's heart to fighting, and I knew that it was the truth.”

The ḥāfiẓ [Ibn Ḥajar] said in al-Fatḥ (1/76): “Some have considered its authenticity unlikely, [arguing] that if Ibn ʿUmar had had the hadith, he would not have left his father disputing with Abū Bakr over fighting those who withheld the zakāh;

and if they had known it, Abū Bakr would not have let ʿUmar argue unchallenged from his words (blessings and peace be upon him), ‘I have been commanded to fight the people until they say there is no god but Allah’, and then turned from arguing with this text to analogy,
when he said: I will certainly fight whoever separates the prayer from the zakāh,

since it is its companion in the Book of Allah. The answer is that Ibn ʿUmar's having the hadith does not mean that he recalled it in that situation; and even if he recalled it, it is possible that he was not present at that debate,

and it is not impossible that he mentioned it to them afterwards. Nor did Abū Bakr rely on analogy alone in fighting those who withheld the zakāh; he also drew it from his words (blessings and peace be upon him) in the hadith that he narrated, ‘except by the right of Islam’,

for Abū Bakr said: And zakāh is the right of Islam. Nor was Ibn ʿUmar alone in narrating the hadith; Abū Hurayrah also narrated it with the addition of the prayer and zakāh, as will be discussed, if Allah the Exalted wills, in the Book of Zakāh.

The story contains evidence that a Sunnah may be hidden from some of the senior Companions while individual Companions know of it. For this reason, opinions are not to be heeded, however strong, when there is a Sunnah that contradicts them, and it is not to be said: How could this have been hidden from so-and-so? And Allah is the One who grants success.”

Excepted from the general command to fight people until they do what is mentioned in the hadith are the People of the Book if they pay the jizyah, as the Qurʾān indicates, and others if they pay it, as the Sunnah indicates,

as in the long hadith of Buraydah ibn al-Ḥuṣayb in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim (1731), which begins: “Whenever the Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed a commander over an army or a raiding party, he would advise him personally to fear Allah and to treat well the Muslims with him…”, to the end of the hadith.

The two testimonies suffice for entering Islam, and they are the first obligation on the legally responsible person. No attention is to be paid to the views of the theologians (mutakallimūn) who rely on other things, such as rational inquiry or the intention to undertake inquiry. Ibn Daqīq al-ʿĪd said in his explanation of this hadith:

“It contains clear evidence for the position of the verifying scholars and the great majority of the earlier and later generations, that if a person believes in the religion of Islam with firm belief, free of doubt, that suffices him, and he is not obliged to learn the proofs of the theologians and to know Allah through them.”
Fighting over withholding the zakāh applies to whoever withholds it and fights over it; if he does not fight, it is taken from him by force.

His words, “and their reckoning is with Allah”, mean that whoever shows Islam outwardly and utters the two testimonies has his wealth and blood protected. If he is truthful outwardly and inwardly, that benefits him with Allah;
but if his inward state differs from his outward one and he showed it out of hypocrisy, he is among the people of the lowest depth of the Fire.
Fighting is commanded until the two testimonies, the prayer and the zakāh are established.
Speech can be called “doing”,
since he said, “If they do that”, and among what he mentioned before it are the two testimonies, which are words.
The reckoning for deeds on the Day of Resurrection is affirmed.
Whoever refuses to pay the zakāh is fought over withholding it until he pays it.
Whoever shows Islam outwardly has it accepted from him, and his inner state is left to Allah.
The two testimonies are inseparable, and both together are indispensable.
The prayer and the zakāh are of great importance: the prayer is the right due from the body, and the zakāh the right due on wealth.
